name: Mansoor Delane
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Sticky man-cover corner with a physical presence on the outside
+ Reactive athleticism; reads receivers and route combinations
+ Smooth moving backward and triggering downhill, and it shows up in run defence
+ Locates the football and attacks it with regularity
+ Football IQ to play zone at a high level
- Lets his eyes wander from zone responsibilities
- Pursuit angles and tackling technique need work downhill
- Needs patience reading quick receivers in soft press
• B/R grade 8.2 — impact player, 1st round; No. 8 overall, CB1
• Pro comparison: Quinyon Mitchell
• 6ft 0in, 190 lb; transferred from Virginia Tech; 4.35 forty at LSU pro day
• Career-high 11 passes defensed in his final season
• Chiefs traded up with Cleveland to take him at No. 6

name: Peter Woods
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Good size with impressive movement skills and quickness for a defensive tackle
+ Upper-body strength and excellent hand placement to control blocks
+ Very good at getting off blocks — stack-and-shed looks easy for him
+ Handles double teams by attacking his assignment, and can split combo blocks
+ Athleticism and power to develop into a pass-rusher
- Minimal pass-rush production: five sacks in 35 career games
- Pad level off the line is subpar, which blunts his bull rush
- Balance when shedding blocks leads to missed tackles
- Weight management — admitted to playing too heavy in 2024
• B/R grade 7.8 — key contributor, 2nd round; No. 31 overall, DL3
• Pro comparison: Jeffery Simmons
• 6ft 3in, 298 lb; four-star recruit in the 2023 class
• Freshman All-American; first-team All-ACC in 2025
• 2025: 30 tackles, 3.5 TFL, 2 sacks

name: R Mason Thomas
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Change-of-direction, suddenness and physicality — very good at turning speed to power
+ Keeps his feet moving through contact to collapse the pocket
+ Good bend and angles, taking efficient paths to the quarterback
+ Non-stop motor with a spin move to get back into the rush
- Lack of arm length limits extension, so he struggles to escape or shed
- Lacks NFL size and length at 6ft 2in, 241 lb
• Projects as a productive third-down rusher
• 2024: nine sacks and 12.5 TFL, second-team All-SEC
• Missed seven games with high-ankle sprains as an underclassman
• Four-star recruit out of Fort Lauderdale in the 2022 class

name: Jadon Canady
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Builds his game around whatever the defence needs from him
+ Genuinely versatile — experience at safety, nickel and outside corner
+ Jitterbug energy level and real physicality
+ Consistently triggers downhill to the football
- Undersized for the outside
- Tackling angles are high and low on the ball carrier, and he misses a lot
- Overly aggressive — opens up quickly in man coverage
- Bites on manipulation, leaving him open to double moves and release packages
• Tailor-made nickel corner who can take that role immediately
• Career-high 12 passes defensed in 2024 at Ole Miss
• Former three-star recruit and three-star transfer

name: Emmett Johnson
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Quick, decisive runner who gets downhill fast
+ Patient, with great vision to find running lanes
+ Acceleration and burst to explode through a crease once it opens
+ Runs inside zone, outside zone and duo concepts well, and reads his keys
+ Low centre of gravity and good contact balance — runs through arm tackles
- Chases the big play outside instead of planting and getting upfield
- Will try to jump cut one too many times
- Speed is good rather than great; not a constant threat to take it the distance
• Andy Reid compared him to LeSean McCoy
• Former three-star recruit in the 2022 class

name: Cyrus Allen
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Three-level receiver and a natural separator
+ Gets open quickly and efficiently
+ Elusive movement patterns that routinely beat man coverage
+ Outstanding route-runner
+ Fearless working underneath and over the middle
- Under 6ft and 183 lb
- Well-travelled — three schools across his college career
• Area scout Cassidy Kaminski: mainly a slot receiver, but can win at the line outside
• Averaged 16.2 yards per catch across his college career
• 13 receiving touchdowns in his final season
• Louisiana Tech, then Texas A&M, then Cincinnati

name: Garrett Nussmeier
evaluation:
Remarks:
+ Natural thrower and a pro-ready timing and rhythm quarterback
+ Accuracy, ball placement and anticipation are his A-traits
+ Sees the field well and delivers catchable passes at all three levels
+ High football IQ — pre-snap checks, route adjustments, sliding protections
+ More athletic than he looks; evades edge pressure with his eyes downfield
- Gunslinger streak — tests occupied windows and puts the ball in harm's way
- A serious core injury led to poor mechanics and bad habits
- Passes lose steam when he is forced to roll to his weak side
• Excellent fit for a quick-passing, West Coast system
• 2025: 1,927 yards, 12 TD, 5 INT in nine games at 67.4 per cent
• Reported cyst on his spine affected his draft stock
• 6ft 2in, 205 lb; slid to the seventh round at 24 years old
